correctness.rationale: Complete algebraic proof for \(n\ge6\) and \(1\le k\le n-3\). The unit disk is Löwner iff positive contact weights have the first two Fourier harmonics zero. Reflection gives \(\mathbb Ec=0\), \(\mathbb Ec^2=1/2\) on the exact cosine interval \([-B,C]\). The bound \(\mathbb Ec^2\le BC\) rules out \(3(k+1)>n\); conversely parity analysis gives \(BC\ge1/2\) if \(3(k+1)\le n\). Two explicit positive zero-mean distributions with second moments on opposite sides of \(1/2\) interpolate to a valid contact certificate; global optimality and strict reverse area follow. Diagnostics cover 60,375 finite parameter pairs through \(n=350\), with 20,010 constructive positive certificates, plus separate 10,875 finite linear-program cases; they are not the infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The surviving-vertex set is fixed, with no freedom to choose a different polygon. A claim that every surviving subset of size at least \(2n/3\) works would be false for arbitrary scattered deletions; contiguity is essential. The equivalence of the disk question to moment feasibility is known. The new nontrivial implication is moment feasibility iff \(3(k+1)\le n\), proved by extremal one-dimensional cosine variance and a constructive interpolation. Generic optimality criteria do not directly subsume this uniform threshold.

value.rationale: A natural robustness invariant of the canonical regular n-gon minimal circumscribed ellipse is determined exactly for arbitrary lengths of a contiguous deleted vertex block. The sharp maximal erasure tolerance \(\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1\) has a nontrivial parity-sensitive proof and sparse constructive isotropic designs, and its threshold asymptotically erases one third of the vertices. The classification is a structural global condition rather than a routine single-polygon instance. Relevance extends to exact degree-two positive cubature on incomplete root-of-unity grids; general formulas for the optimizer beyond the threshold are not claimed.
